bugs.description: collection-all? returns #f immediately if a block is missing, whereas collection-any? skips missing blocks. This inconsistency makes collection-all? fail for collections with missing blocks even if all available blocks satisfy the predicate.
bugs.fix_suggestion:
Modify collection-all? to skip missing blocks, similar to collection-any?, fold-collection, and filter-collection. 
(if block
    (if (predicate block) (loop (cdr hashes)) #f)
    (loop (cdr hashes)))

bugs.description: collection-group-by has O(N*G) complexity where G is the number of groups. It iterates the groups list with 'map' for every element to update the group, resulting in quadratic behavior for collections with many unique keys.
bugs.code_snippet:
(map (lambda (pair)
             (if (equal? (car pair) key)
                 (cons key (cons block (cdr pair)))
                 pair))
     groups)
bugs.fix_suggestion: Use a hash table to accumulate groups during iteration, then convert to an association list at the end for O(N) performance.

bugs.description: topological-sort documentation claims it returns 'dependencies before dependents', which implies a reverse topological sort (build order). However, the implementation returns a standard topological sort (dependents before dependencies, i.e., parent before child).
bugs.code_snippet:
;;; Returns sorted list of hashes (dependencies before dependents)
...
(set! result (cons node result))
bugs.fix_suggestion: Clarify the documentation to match the behavior (dependents before dependencies) or reverse the result list if build order is intended.

bugs.description: subgraph function has O(N * M) complexity where N is subgraph size and M is list size, due to using linear scan (hash-in-list?) inside the loop. This scales poorly for large subgraphs.
bugs.fix_suggestion: Convert hash-list to a hash table (set) at the start of the function and use O(1) lookups for filtering neighbors.

bugs.description: collection-remove removes ALL instances of a block hash. Since collection-add allows duplicates (bag semantics), removing all instances when only one removal might be expected is a potential logic error or at least inconsistent with typical bag operations.
bugs.fix_suggestion: If bag semantics are intended, remove only the first occurrence of the hash. If set semantics are intended, collection-add should prevent duplicates.

summary: Verified the known inconsistency in collection-all?. Found performance issues in collection grouping and subgraph extraction due to inefficient list lookups. Identified a discrepancy between documentation and implementation in topological-sort order.
